items.q: The cardiovascular system in CKD is the:
items.exp: CKD - cardiovascular system: leading cause of mortality. (Book p814)

items.q: In ESRD patients, what share of deaths is due to cardiac causes?
items.exp: ESRD patients: 50% due to cardiac causes. (Book p814)

items.q: A young patient with CKD carries what fold risk of cardiac disease compared to the control population?
items.exp: Young patient with CKD: 500 fold risk of cardiac disease compared to control population. (Book p814)

items.q: Match the following non-traditional cause to its effect — 1) Uremic toxins  2) Endothelial dysfunction  3) LVH  4) Malnutrition-inflammation-nephrosclerosis … A) ADMA ↑ → ↓ NO; loss of fetuin  B) Uremic cardiomyopathy  C) HF with preserved EF  D) Insulin resistance; protein-energy malnutrition
items.exp: Non-traditional causes: uremic toxins (uremic cardiomyopathy); medial calcification; LVH (HF with preserved EF); endothelial dysfunction (ADMA ↑ → ↓ NO, loss of fetuin); malnutrition-inflammation-nephrosclerosis (insulin resistance, protein-energy malnutrition). (Book p814)

items.q: ADMA, which rises in endothelial dysfunction, stands for:
items.exp: Endothelial dysfunction: ADMA ↑ → ↓ NO (asymmetric dimethylarginine); loss of fetuin. (Book p814)

items.q: The arterial features of CVD in CKD are:
opts: Endothelial dysfunction, medial calcification, ↑ wall thickness
Intimal atherosclerosis, vasculitis and aneurysm formation
Medial atrophy with a fall in wall thickness
items.exp: Arteries: endothelial dysfunction; medial calcification; ↑ wall thickness. (Book p814)

items.q: The arterial consequences in the same list are:
opts: ↑ carotid systolic BP and ↓ augmented pulse velocity
↓ carotid systolic BP and ↑ augmented pulse velocity
items.exp: ↑ carotid systolic BP; ↓ augmented pulse velocity. (Book p814)

items.q: The cardiac features of CVD in CKD are:
opts: LVH, myocardial fibrosis and uremic cardiomyopathy
Mitral stenosis, aortic regurgitation, pericardial effusion
items.exp: Heart: LVH; myocardial fibrosis; uremic cardiomyopathy. (Book p814)

items.q: All but one are the six overlapping circles in the CKD-CV flower diagram. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Circles: CKD-MBD, endothelial dysfunction, protein carbamylation, oxidative stress, uremic toxins, gut dysbiosis. (Book p814)

items.q: The CVD treatment principle is to start early therapies — which trio is listed?
opts: Early dialysis, adequate phosphate binders early, transplant before calcification sets in
Late dialysis, calcium binders late, transplant after calcification sets in
Iron first, ESA second, transplant last in the sequence
Surgery, stents and calcitonin in sequence
items.exp: Start early therapies: early dialysis; adequate phosphate binders in early stage of disease; transplant before calcification sets in. (Book p814)
Uremia can cause: pericarditis; hyperkalemia → arrhythmias. (Book p814)

items.q: Hyperkalemia from uremia can lead to arrhythmias.
The best marker for MI in CKD patients is:
items.exp: MI in CKD: best marker — Trop-I (rate of rise). (Book p814)

items.q: The most specific troponin I rise pattern is:
The pre-requisites for renal transplant include which set?
opts: Iliac vessel doppler, peripheral artery doppler, CT for calcification
Coronary angiogram first, then echocardiography and stress test
Renal biopsy, HLA typing, PPD and donor serology
CT angiography of the aorta, stress test and TTE
items.exp: Pre-requisite for renal transplant: iliac vessel doppler; peripheral artery doppler; CT for calcification → normal → coronary angiogram. (Book p814)

items.q: After a normal doppler and CT work-up, the next investigation in the transplant chain is:
items.exp: CT for calcification → normal → coronary angiogram. (Book p814)

items.q: All but one feed the 'elevated oxidative stress' hub in the sources diagram. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Sources: malnutrition; bacterial products in dialysate; chronic kidney disease; interactions between blood and membrane; loss of antioxidants during dialysis. (Book p814)

items.q: A CKD patient with chest pain has a troponin I that rises 20% over 9 hours. This pattern is:
opts: The most specific MI marker pattern
items.exp: Trop-I rate of rise: ↑20% in 9 hours (most specific). (Book p814)
